mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1) and monthly changes in retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust demand transmission, which supports higher corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(r) between monthly ΔGDPC1 and monthly ΔRSAFS > 0.7 over the last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when the 6-month correlation between ΔGDPC1 and ΔRSAFS exceeds 0.7.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction and materials sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months and monetary policy is not easing.
